label: Harzer Rotvieh

about.text: The Harzer Rotvieh is a red German cattle breed from the Harz mountains, used for milk, beef and draught work. Since 1980 it has been treated as only a variety of the Angeln breed, and in the mid-1980s its remaining animals were used to build the Rotes Höhenvieh population.

sources.text: Origin, uses, the 1980 Angeln variety status and the Rotes Höhenvieh history, from the Wikipedia article (fetched with WebFetch).

origin.place: The Harz mountains, Germany. The article says it stemmed from the red cattle breeds of South and Middle Germany.

sources.text: Place of origin and descent from the red Germanic cattle, from the Wikipedia article (fetched with WebFetch). No formation dates are given for the breed itself, so none are entered.
The article lists the uses as milk, beef and draught power.

facts.v: Crossed with Danish Red bulls in the 1950s to raise milk yields, and afterwards crossed with Angeln cattle.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article (fetched with WebFetch). The Angeln crossing has no date in the article.

gaps: Searched for a DAD-IS entry, a population figure, milk yield and a risk status. None was found: DAD-IS did not turn up its own entry, and the Wikipedia article gives only two small herd counts with no years. A Saxon state document gives 2,423 herdbook cows, but for the wider Rotes Höhenvieh group, not this breed alone, so it is left out. Alternate names: none found beyond the German name. Formation dates: not given.
